Position Summary
Training Officers work in a dynamic vocational, education and training environment in which they have to adapt and be responsive to changes in national curriculum, the VET Quality Framework, technological developments and a diversity and breadth of client training demands.

The role of the Training Officer embraces the extent of the learning process from program enquiry/advice through to assessing and determining the training requirements of clients, following onto managing the learning process for clients using a variety of training strategies including recognition of prior learning, recognition of current competencies, training delivery, workplace learning, delivery and assessment, formal assessment and reporting etc..  

The training Officer will have the vocational skills in the area that they are applying for with a minimum of three to five years’ experience in their chosen vocational area.

The Training Officer ideally would have at least have obtained the following competencies from the Training and Assessment Training Package or is able to demonstrate equivalent competencies. However if the candidate does not have these competencies or the full Training & Assessment Qualification they will agree to work with an accredited assessor until this qualification is achieved.

The Training Officer is expected to be innovative in responding effectively to the training demands of clients.  The Training Officer works in a wide variety of learning environments providing a range of flexible training and learning strategies to best meet the client needs including flexible delivery, workplace training and assessment, training room delivery, on line learning support etc.   

The Training Officer will be expected to be able to work effectively as a member of a team and be required to be involved in a range of course/program coordination and administration activities that support the effective operation of the company and the achievement of learning outcomes for participants.  

POSITION PARAMETERS
1.	SUPERVISION AND ACCOUNTABILITY The position reports to the Manager and may work in a number of program areas. 
2.	LOCATION Training Staff are required to work on site or at a designated training facility.  
3.	PARTICIPATION ON COMMITTEES Training Officers are required to attend program meetings and team meetings, or other external committees as required.

Duty Statement
1.	Develop and manage the learning process for participants. 
2.	Train in a range of subjects and programs in a variety of learning modes at locations specified by the Manager. (See Attachment 1 for position details)
3.	Prepare quality learning and assessment resources within the context of established curriculum, training packages under the national framework, competency standards, the diversity of students and client’s requirements. Unless otherwise agreed with the Training Officer, Intellectual Property in all material developed or produced shall remain within Industry Training & Workplace Services.
4.	Participate as a member of a team on a range of tasks including curriculum and program development, program delivery, professional development, marketing activities and administrative and operational functions.
5.	Undertake, where required, course coordination and a range of planning tasks relevant to the delivery of quality courses.
6.	Provide support and advice to participants of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities and implement appropriate support strategies and/or learning programs and strategies as required.
7.	Undertake as required a range of participant support service tasks to ensure the effective operation of the Company, for example participant selection, course advice, enrolment and telephone enquiry support.
8.	Research, adapt and develop innovative learning practices and delivery options that enhance the Company's capacity to meet the demands of participants. 
9.	Manage the delivery of training services to industry, including workplace visits, assessing training needs, developing training plans and coordinating the effective delivery of programs.
10.	Participate in and contribute to the development and implementation of evaluation and continuous improvement processes across the Company.
11.	Undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional and vocational competencies as a Training Officer.
12.	Comply with the quality assurance requirements of the Australian Quality Training Framework and the company’s Quality System.

SELECTION CRITERIA 
Qualifications
1.	The minimum training qualification is the Certificate IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent. 
2.	It is mandatory to have relevant vocational competence at or higher than the level being delivered or assessed through having qualifications and/or relevant industry experience. 
3.	Training Officers who do not hold the minimum or equivalent training qualification must undertake professional development to gain the training qualification within 12 months of commencement. In the interim, the training officer must agree to be mentored by a qualified Trainer who does hold the minimum or equivalent qualification

Training Excellence
1.	Demonstrated excellence in training, management of learning and assessment.
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to development of learning resources.
3.	 An understanding of current developments and innovative approaches in training.
4.	Demonstrated experience, or ability to, develop and conduct training programs suitable to the needs of industry.
5.	Demonstrated record of innovation in training and proven commitment to undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional competence.

Communication Skills
1.	Proven ability to operate effectively as a member of a team.
2.	High level interpersonal and communication skills.
3.	Demonstrated ability to provide support and advice to students of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities.
Administration
1.	High level organisational skills
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to the overall functioning of the company including record keeping, course maintenance and quality improvement and ability to use all relevant technology.

Further Information
For further information please contact Toni Hoyle.
Telephone 90227100 or 0419 908 425

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Requisition ID: REQ676680
Employment Type: Permanent Part Time- Full Time working 38 hours per week
Remuneration: $41.22 - $57.88 per week + 12% Superannuation +Salary Packaging
Located in: Liverpool Hospital
Applications close: 26-07-2026
Contact: Amanda Rehayem - Midwifery Unit Manager | Midwifery Models of Care Liverpool Hospital, Women's and Children's Health | 0455 993 666 | Amanda.Rehayem@health.nsw.gov.au | 

Please note: A current influenza (flu) vaccination is a mandatory requirement for appointment to this position. 

 

With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we're enriching health, and develop your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia. 
 

Achieve Something Great 
Join our Midwifery Support Program (MSP) Hybrid Model and play a vital role in extending compassionate, high-quality care beyond the hospital setting. In this rewarding community-based position, you will provide postnatal care to women and their newborns in their homes for up to 14 days following birth, supporting families during one of life's most significant transitions.

Working autonomously within a supportive multidisciplinary framework, you will conduct comprehensive maternal and newborn assessments, provide breastfeeding and infant feeding support, deliver education tailored to individual family needs, and identify and escalate clinical concerns where required. Your practice will promote safe recovery, early parenting confidence, and seamless continuity between hospital and community services.

This role offers the opportunity to build meaningful short-term therapeutic relationships, empower families in their own environments, and contribute to positive early parenting outcomes. With a strong focus on woman-centred, culturally responsive care, you will combine clinical expertise with empathy, flexibility and strong organisational skills to manage a dynamic daily schedule across the community. As part of the MSP team, you will be supported by your colleagues and the Midwifery Unit Manager of models of care at Liverpool Hospital.

If you are a motivated Registered Midwife who values autonomy, continuity, and making a tangible difference in the early postnatal period, this is an exceptional opportunity to grow your practice in a highly impactful community-based model of care. 

Are You the Right Fit? 
Success in this position comes from bringing a thoughtful combination of clinical expertise, sound judgement and personal qualities that support safe, compassionate and collaborative midwifery practice, as reflected in the attributes outlined below.

Specific Skills & Qualifications-Role requirements

Unrestricted current registration as a midwife with AHPRA

Availability and capacity to work on a rotating roster across weekdays and weekends including public holidays

Current unrestricted NSW Drivers Licence (P2 Licence Acceptable) and willingness to travel in the course of employment

Demonstrated experience in antenatal, intrapartum and postnatal care -student midwifery experience will be considered. MSP experience desirable but not mandatory. 

Ability to work autonomously and collaboratively with midwifery and multidisciplinary team members and apply professional and ethical boundaries.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills

Engagement in professional development and team meetings and huddles as required 

Role entails

Conducting comprehensive maternal and newborn postnatal assessments in the home 

Monitoring maternal recovery, newborn wellbeing, and newborn weight progress

Providing breastfeeding and infant feeding support and education

Delivering tailored education on newborn care, maternal health and adjustment-transition to parenting

Identifying clinical risks and pathologies such as jaundice, feeding difficulties or postnatal mental health concerns and escalating appropriately 

Maintaining accurate and timely documentation on the electronic medical record (eMR) 

Liaising with hospital teams, child and family health services and GPs as required

Managing a daily schedule of community visits across a designated area 

Triaging daily MSP intake from the postnatal ward 

Selection Criteria 
To help us assess your suitability for the role, please tell us as much as you can about yourself in response to the questions below. 

Do you have current Authority to Practice as a Registered Midwife with Australian Health Practitioners Regulation Agency (AHPRA)? Please attach a copy of your AHPRA registration in your application

Describe your experience in providing postnatal and newborn care in either a hospital or community setting. How do you assess and respond to clinical concerns in the first 14 days postpartum?

Working in the MSP requires autonomous practice in women's homes. Can you provide an example of how you have managed your workload independently while maintaining effective communication and collaboration with the broader healthcare team?

Do you have a current Australian C-Class driver's license (including P1 or P2)? if you hold a C class license (P1 or P2 included) from a state other than NSW must obtain a NSW C class (P1 or P2 included) license within three months of appointment. Learner's licenses are not permitted. 

If you'd like more details, we're here to help.

Aboriginal Workforce

One extra day off each month for full-time employees

Access to learning opportunities through our dedicated Education and Organisational Development team, who support staff with training, workshops, and career

The role of the Training Officer embraces the extent of the learning process from program enquiry/advice through to assessing and determining the training requirements of clients, following onto managing the learning process for clients using a variety of training strategies including recognition of prior learning, recognition of current competencies, training delivery, workplace learning, delivery and assessment, formal assessment and reporting etc..  

The training Officer will have the vocational skills in the area that they are applying for with a minimum of three to five years’ experience in their chosen vocational area.

The Training Officer ideally would have at least have obtained the following competencies from the Training and Assessment Training Package or is able to demonstrate equivalent competencies. However if the candidate does not have these competencies or the full Training & Assessment Qualification they will agree to work with an accredited assessor until this qualification is achieved.

The Training Officer is expected to be innovative in responding effectively to the training demands of clients.  The Training Officer works in a wide variety of learning environments providing a range of flexible training and learning strategies to best meet the client needs including flexible delivery, workplace training and assessment, training room delivery, on line learning support etc.   

The Training Officer will be expected to be able to work effectively as a member of a team and be required to be involved in a range of course/program coordination and administration activities that support the effective operation of the company and the achievement of learning outcomes for participants.  

POSITION PARAMETERS
1.	SUPERVISION AND ACCOUNTABILITY The position reports to the Manager and may work in a number of program areas. 
2.	LOCATION Training Staff are required to work on site or at a designated training facility.  
3.	PARTICIPATION ON COMMITTEES Training Officers are required to attend program meetings and team meetings, or other external committees as required.

Duty Statement
1.	Develop and manage the learning process for participants. 
2.	Train in a range of subjects and programs in a variety of learning modes at locations specified by the Manager. (See Attachment 1 for position details)
3.	Prepare quality learning and assessment resources within the context of established curriculum, training packages under the national framework, competency standards, the diversity of students and client’s requirements. Unless otherwise agreed with the Training Officer, Intellectual Property in all material developed or produced shall remain within Industry Training & Workplace Services.
4.	Participate as a member of a team on a range of tasks including curriculum and program development, program delivery, professional development, marketing activities and administrative and operational functions.
5.	Undertake, where required, course coordination and a range of planning tasks relevant to the delivery of quality courses.
6.	Provide support and advice to participants of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities and implement appropriate support strategies and/or learning programs and strategies as required.
7.	Undertake as required a range of participant support service tasks to ensure the effective operation of the Company, for example participant selection, course advice, enrolment and telephone enquiry support.
8.	Research, adapt and develop innovative learning practices and delivery options that enhance the Company's capacity to meet the demands of participants. 
9.	Manage the delivery of training services to industry, including workplace visits, assessing training needs, developing training plans and coordinating the effective delivery of programs.
10.	Participate in and contribute to the development and implementation of evaluation and continuous improvement processes across the Company.
11.	Undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional and vocational competencies as a Training Officer.
12.	Comply with the quality assurance requirements of the Australian Quality Training Framework and the company’s Quality System.

SELECTION CRITERIA 
Qualifications
1.	The minimum training qualification is the Certificate IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent. 
2.	It is mandatory to have relevant vocational competence at or higher than the level being delivered or assessed through having qualifications and/or relevant industry experience. 
3.	Training Officers who do not hold the minimum or equivalent training qualification must undertake professional development to gain the training qualification within 12 months of commencement. In the interim, the training officer must agree to be mentored by a qualified Trainer who does hold the minimum or equivalent qualification

Training Excellence
1.	Demonstrated excellence in training, management of learning and assessment.
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to development of learning resources.
3.	 An understanding of current developments and innovative approaches in training.
4.	Demonstrated experience, or ability to, develop and conduct training programs suitable to the needs of industry.
5.	Demonstrated record of innovation in training and proven commitment to undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional competence.

Communication Skills
1.	Proven ability to operate effectively as a member of a team.
2.	High level interpersonal and communication skills.
3.	Demonstrated ability to provide support and advice to students of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities.
Administration
1.	High level organisational skills
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to the overall functioning of the company including record keeping, course maintenance and quality improvement and ability to use all relevant technology.

Further Information

In the remote outback community of Wudinna, the work of a Community Support Worker carries real weight. At Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN), you'll be the person who helps someone stay in the home they love - offering practical support, genuine connection, and the kind of care that makes independence possible. This casual position is available until 30 June 2027.

What You'll Be Doing

Working within EFNLHN's Consumer Directed Care model, you'll deliver support tailored to each client's goals and preferences - because here, the consumer shapes the care. Shifts, duties, and frequency are guided by the people you support, giving your work real purpose and variety.

Assist clients with personal hygiene, grooming, and mobility in a respectful and dignified manner

Perform household tasks including cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and minor gardening

Provide reliable transport to appointments and community outings

Support social engagement and activities that contribute to client wellbeing

At the WHD4 level, deliver personal care to clients with more complex support needs

What You'll Bring

A warm, empathetic approach and the confidence to work independently in the community

Sound communication skills and genuine respect for people from diverse cultures and backgrounds

Experience supporting aged, frail, or disabled individuals

Ability to work collaboratively as part of a small, community-based team

For appointment at WHD4 level: Certificate III or higher in Individual Support (Aged Care, Disability, or Home and Community)

An understanding of or willingness to learn the values and priorities of SA Health's person-centred care approach

Why EFNLHN and Wudinna

EFNLHN serves one of South Australia's most geographically expansive regions, and the Wudinna Community and Allied Health team sits at the heart of that mission. As part of SA Health, you'll have access to generous salary packaging benefits that meaningfully increase your take-home pay, along with the professional support of a broader health network behind you. Working in a small, close-knit team in regional SA means your contribution is visible and valued every single day - this isn't a role where your work disappears into a crowd. For those drawn to remote community health, Wudinna offers a genuine sense of belonging and the satisfaction of knowing the people you support.

Ready to Apply?

Submit your application through the SA Health careers portal. For a conversation about the role before applying, reach out to the EFNLHN Wudinna Community and Allied Health team directly. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and from people of all backgrounds and abilities.

About Us

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy. We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Why Join Us

Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.
